parties:
Aynunnahar Siddiqua and Others
Vs.
Government of Bangladesh represented by the secretary, ministry of law, justice and parliamentary affairs, Bangladesh secretariat, Ramna, Dhaka and others''
full_judgment: 26. To be more specific, a reference to Rule 3(4)(kha) of the Rules of 2006 positively indicates that the Police Commissioner of Dhaka is authorized to take any prompt step in thwarting any attempt to disturb the peace and in the interest of maintenance of public safety. This Clause (kha) does not seem to be unqualified. Rather the words— “যে কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ” appear to have been qualified by the words—“শান্তিপূর্ণ অবস্থা বজায় রাখার স্বার্থে” in Rule 3(4)(kha). So we find a sort of guideline in Rule 3(4)(kha) for taking any hurried step in the interest of public safety in the city. The Police Commissioner cannot take any arbitrary or whimsical or irrational or unfair or unjustified step with regard to maintenance of law and order within the territorial limits of Dhaka Metropolitan City by having recourse to the expression “যে কোন পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ” occurring in Rule 3(4)(kha). What we are trying to emphasize is this: the Police Commissioner is empowered by Rule 3(4)(kha) of the Rules of 2006 to take any prompt step in the interest of peace and tranquility in the city. This is, no doubt, a discretionary power given to the Police Commissioner of Dhaka as is evident from Rule 3(4)(kha) itself. When any discretionary power is conferred by a statute, it is presumed that the authority entrusted with the discretion will act bona fide and lawfully [State (Delhi Admn.)...Vs...V.C. Shukla and another, AIR 1980 SC 1382]. There cannot be any presumption that the power so conferred will be misused [Organo Chemical Industries and another .Vs. Union of India and others, AIR 1979 SC 1803].
